=== HEADLINE: THE COMMITTED BEADS LEDGER WAS NON-REBUILDABLE, AND ONLY A FRESH WORKTREE COULD SEE IT ===
Preflight `br sync` in the /tmp worktree aborted hard: 'Database error: internal error: VDBE halted with code 19: PRIMARY KEY constraint failed', leaving .beads/.br_recovery/*.rebuild-failed and NO usable DB. Root cause measured, not guessed: .beads/issues.jsonl at 140521b2 held TWO DIFFERENT COMMENTS BOTH WITH id 3600 -- bd-350ku (created 2026-07-31T22:54:21Z, the ac-tidy Tier-2 evidence comment) and bd-gcrhc (2026-07-31T23:14:47Z, the RustHarbor/SageCove service-worker implementation note). Counts: issue ids 2467 records / 2467 unique = clean; comment ids 3604 total / 3603 unique = exactly this one pair.
WHY IT WENT UNSEEN: the comments table has id as PRIMARY KEY, so only a rebuild-from-JSONL trips it, and every checkout that already holds a working beads.db never re-imports. The breakage is therefore invisible from precisely the places people work, and visible only to a fresh clone or worktree -- i.e. to this heartbeat, and to any new machine or CI job that ever tries to stand the ledger up. It was committed and pushed on 07-31 and survived a full day.
MECHANISM: comment ids are per-DB autoincrement. Two sessions holding separate beads.db files each mint the same next id and the shared JSONL merges both. bd-gcrhc's own attribution note records the concurrency ('a concurrent session in this shared checkout committed ... between my `git add` and my `git commit`'). This is a CLASS that recurs on any concurrent-session night, not a one-off.
REPAIR APPLIED (instance only, deliberately minimal): renumbered bd-gcrhc's comment 3600 -> 3627 (max observed 3626) via a single byte-scoped sed on one line. Lossless -- text, author, timestamp, parent issue all unchanged; only the surrogate key moved. Verified: 0 duplicate comment ids, exactly 1 line differs from the pre-edit file, `br sync` then reports 'Created: 2467 issues', and 0 bead ids present at HEAD went missing (comm check before commit). The generator is NOT fixed; that is bd-9edhn.
JUDGEMENT CALL, FLAGGED FOR REVIEW: repairing a corrupt committed artifact is not in ac-tidy's sanctioned Tier-1 list. It was done because it is a hard blocker -- without it this run could create no proposal beads and do no bead scans at all -- and because the fix is provably lossless and independently verifiable. If Craig disagrees with tidy taking this kind of repair autonomously, say so and the guardrail should name it explicitly either way.

=== TOOLING NOTES ===
(1) NEW AND SEVERE -- see headline. A fresh worktree could not rebuild the beads DB at all because of a duplicate comment id in the committed JSONL. The heartbeat's step-0 rehydrate instruction ('run br sync once so br rebuilds its DB from that JSONL') assumes the rebuild can succeed; it cannot when the ledger is corrupt, and the failure mode is a hard abort, not a degraded import. Recommend the heartbeat add the uniq -d probe from bd-9edhn as an explicit preflight step so a future run diagnoses this in one command instead of five.
(2) `br sync --flush-only` reported 'Nothing to export (no dirty issues)' AFTER label edits and two `br create`s -- br 0.2.16 appears to flush to JSONL eagerly on each mutating command. Not a bug, but the heartbeat's step-0 promise that step 5 'commits the flushed .beads/issues.jsonl' should not depend on an explicit flush succeeding. Verification against the JSONL (which is what the SKILL mandates) caught this immediately; a run trusting the flush command's output would have thought nothing landed.
(3) board-scan.md's br-list-excludes-closed-beads warning (added after 08-01) is now correct and load-bearing, and it saved time tonight. Keep it. Same for the literal-scratch-path note on Scans D and E -- dcg blocked the `$D/...` form again exactly as documented, and the literal /tmp/ac_board_scan_scratch/ path ran clean.
(4) jq's fromdateiso8601 REJECTS the fractional-second timestamps br writes ('2026-07-22T08:29:43.577266Z' -> 'does not match format'). Any age/staleness computation over created_at must strip the fraction first (`sub("\\.[0-9]+";"")`). Cost one failed finding-lane scan. Worth a line in board-scan.md next to the other br gotchas.
(5) slack-send still has NO --dry-run (SEVENTH night reporting). The probe in heartbeat step 0 errors out with 'unrecognized arguments: --dry-run' and exit 0, which is a misleading pair. Heartbeat should just say 'read infrastructure/slack/channels.json'.
(6) `git commit -- <pathspec>` still fails on untracked files ('did not match any file(s) known to git'), so _plans/_proposals/<date>/ needs an explicit scoped `git add` first (SEVENTH night; heartbeat step 5 still silent on it). Note the failed commit still exits 0, so a run that trusts the exit code will believe it committed and then push 'Everything up-to-date' -- exactly what happened here before the retry. That is a silent-stranding hazard the push-verify in step 6 does catch, but only after the fact.
(7) last-run.json still requires the Write tool -- the heredoc redirect is blocked by dcg core.filesystem:redirect-truncate-root-home (SEVENTH night), and Write additionally requires a Read of the file first.
(8) The `.claude/skills/ac-tidy` relative symlink is broken from inside a /tmp worktree exactly as the heartbeat warns; SKILL.md and this file were both read/written via $BCA. The caveat is correct and load-bearing -- keep it.
